## Identity correspondences — How do we match people and vessels, and construct ROS trip IDs? {#identity-correspondences-how-do-we-match-people-and-vessels-and-construct-ros-trip-ids}

Agree how to match people and vessels and construct the ROS trip identifier.

Define the handling of missing or ambiguous matches.

Use the [shared mapping design](../03-references/mapping-design.html) for the generic lookup mechanism.

## Match ObServe registries to ROS registries

Registry matching identifies the same person or vessel in two systems, rather than translating a code's meaning.

First resolve the extracted ObServe ID in `common.person` or `common.vessel` to obtain the source record.

Then identify the corresponding record in the ROS registry selected by the target field.

| Source record                  | Target record        | Matching approach                                         |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `common.person`, observer role | ROS observer         | Use an agreed identifier correspondence where available.   |
| `common.vessel`                | ROS vessel           | Prefer its IOTC ID, checked against the target registry.    |

For people, do not assume that `common.person.code` is an IOTC observer identifier.

A person can have several ObServe roles. The field mapping determines which ROS registry and role are relevant.

Other vessel identifiers may support matching only when their meaning and target lookup are explicitly agreed.

Name matching can help when a reliable identifier is unavailable, using the configured ROS name lookup.

A unique name match is a candidate identity match, not proof that two records identify the same entity.

The sheet review must define when that fallback is acceptable and what additional information must agree.

Require one accepted target record. Do not choose arbitrarily when several records match.

Write the required ROS identifier from that record, preserving the ObServe ID in the mapping trace.

Do not invent identifiers for missing matches, such as a placeholder observer number.

Explicit identity correspondences belong to the mapping and retain the registry data’s access controls.

Do not place private person or vessel mappings in public package files or in the public code-list catalogue.

The storage format and lookup for any explicit ObServe-to-ROS identity correspondence remain to be defined.

Reuse accepted identity matches across trips that refer to the same source record.
